title: Hash-sketch sampler with deferred exemplar rehydration
creator: Asha Patel
description: Introduce a low-cost on-hotpath sketch-based sampler that records a compact hash-key and tiny metadata on every request, and then defers expensive exemplar reconstruction and encoding to a background reconciler. The goal is to drastically reduce CPU and allocation pressure in the inference hot path while preserving the ability to reconstruct representative traces for tail analysis and perf regressions. This work targets services with QPS > 5k where current trace overhead contributes >6% p99 latency variance.
acceptance_criteria: Hotpath allocation per request reduced by >= 40% compared to current sampler on 4 GPU pods
p50/p95 latency impact from tracing in synthetic benchmark <= 1% relative increase
End-to-end exemplar recovery accuracy >= 90% for sampled tail traces (as measured by match on span chain IDs and key attributes)
No regressions in existing tracing dashboards or billing metrics after rollout
tasks: Design compact sketch format (64-bit hash + 1 byte flags + 2 byte route id) — draft spec
Implement hotpath writer that appends sketch entries into lock-free ring buffer
Implement background reconciler that consumes sketches, retrieves full metadata from ephemeral cache, reconstructs exemplars and emits full spans
Add feature flag + config for per-service sampling thresholds and late-resolution window
Add unit + integration tests for sketch collisions and late resolution corner cases
Benchmark on staging with representative traffic (batch sizes, seq len distribution)
Create rollout dashboard and SLO alerts, then canary rollout to 10% -> 50% -> 100%
progress_updates: 2025-02-18: Design spec v0.1 reviewed with Observability and Runtime teams, agreed on 64-bit hash and 16-bit tag space to reduce collisions
2025-02-24: Prototype hotpath writer implemented; microbenchmarks show 2.3x lower allocations on synthetic hotpath compared to baseline sampler
2025-03-01: Background reconciler MVP implemented and wired to async emitter; initial exemplar recovery works on simple traces but fails when ephemeral cache TTL is too short
2025-03-04: Increased cache TTL to 120s in staging; exemplar recovery rate improved to ~92% during tail replays
review_feedback: Infra review: prefer lock-free buffers sized per-shard to avoid cross-core contention (see PR comments)
Security: ensure no user PII is stored in sketches — limit fields to non-PII route ids and hashkeys (conformance added)
PM: add opt-out knob for customers with strict compliance requirements
SRE: add circuit breaker to stop background reconciler if backlog grows beyond threshold to protect control plane
rollout_plan: Feature-gated rollout: enable on internal staging; canary at 10% of production traffic for 48h with automated rollback if service.p95 increases >2% or reconcilier backlog > 10k. Expand to 50% for 72h, then 100% if stable. Provide a manual override to revert per-tenant.
risks: Hash collision causing exemplar mix-up for small fraction of traces; mitigated by adding route id and 64-bit hash
If background reconciler falls behind, we may lose exemplar fidelity temporarily; plan includes backlog alerts and circuit breaker
Long-tail queries that rely on immediate exemplar availability (e.g., realtime debugging) may observe delay — documented in console
Edge-case: ephemeral cache misses due to pod restarts — reconciler will mark those sketches as unresolved and emit a minimal span instead
qa_plan: Run unit tests for sketch encoding/decoding, fuzz-test collision scenarios, run integration tests that replay synthesized tail traces and check exemplar recovery. Load test at 2x expected QPS and verify no increase in p99 > 1.5% and allocator profiles show expected reduction.
notes: This approach aims to strike a practical balance: minimal hotpath footprint while preserving posthoc trace reconstruction for engineering investigations. If reconciler accuracy is unacceptable, fallback will be a per-route hybrid where high-risk routes keep full hotpath spans. Will coordinate with Console team to expose 'exemplar availability' status in trace UI.
